description: The bar chart illustrates the accuracy (%) of a multimodal misinformation detection model across two datasets—PHEME and PolitiFact—under various ablation conditions, comparing the full model (“Ours”) against variants that remove specific components such as text, comment context, selection mechanism, emotion modeling, or cognitive features. On the PHEME dataset, the full model achieves 89.84% accuracy, outperforming ablated versions: “w/o text” (86.82%), “w/o select” (80.10%), “w/o emotion” (88.80%), and “w/o cognition” (87.17%). On PolitiFact, the full model reaches 90.57% accuracy, again surpassing ablated variants: “w/o comments” (85.85%), “w/o text” (83.02%), “w/o select” (89.62%), “w/o emotion” (84.91%), and “w/o cognition” (87.74%). The chart uses distinct colors for each condition and labels each bar with its exact accuracy value; the y-axis ranges from 75.0% to 95.0% in 0.5% increments. The “w/o select” condition shows the largest performance drop in both datasets, indicating the critical role of the selection mechanism, while “w/o emotion” and “w/o cognition” also significantly degrade performance, supporting the paper’s emphasis on integrating cognitive and emotional cues for effective misinformation detection.
